title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a long computation in the post-Longue-Marche notes (pp. 650 bis–787). The setting appears to be the profinite/arithmetic structure attached to SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, its congruence quotient mod 12 (the abelianization of SL2(Z) is Z/12), and automorphisms of an elliptic curve C_K over a field K.

Section 4 introduces a group N_{ρ,σ} (first written as Z̃_{ρ,σ}, then corrected). It fits into an exact sequence 1 → N^{0+}_{ρ,σ} → N_{ρ,σ} → 𝔒_12^* → 1, with a pointer to GL(2, Z/12Z).

The group is realized as a subobject of 𝔒_12^* × M × M (eq. 94). Here M is apparently a rank-2 lattice or the corresponding vector group scheme. Its points are triples (M, α0, β0) satisfying the inhomogeneous linear condition
(1 − ρ_M)(α0) − (1 − σ_M)(β0) = 3 ν''(M) λ1.

- ρ_M and σ_M are the images of the two 'elliptic' generators (orders 3 or 6, and 4 or 2) twisted by M.
- ν''(M) is the integer-valued 'parity' function from the previous page (eq. 90–93), which vanishes when M = 1.

This is the standard shape of a 1-cocycle or crossed-homomorphism condition on an amalgam generated by ρ and σ. A cocycle is given by its values (α0, β0) on the two generators, subject to compatibility on the common subgroup. The right-hand side 3ν''λ1 is a twisting term, which makes the group an extension of 𝔒_12^* rather than a semidirect product.

Eq. (95) uses (1 − ρ)(λ1 − λ0) = 3λ1. This is the Eisenstein-type identity (1 − ρ)(1 − ρ²) = 3 for ρ of order 3, with λ0 = ρ²λ1. Substituting it shows the twisting term is a coboundary-like shift: condition (94) becomes the homogeneous form (96),
(1 − ρ_M)(α0 − ν''(λ1 − λ0)) − (1 − σ_M)(β0) = 0.

Grothendieck then admits without proof a natural group structure on Z̃_{ρ,σ} for which the projection to 𝔒_12^* is a homomorphism. This gives the exact sequence (97), whose kernel (98) is the linear group scheme {(α0, β0) | (1 − ρ)α0 = (1 − σ)β0}.

The final remark is that this group scheme over Spec Z is smooth away from 3 but not in characteristic 3. The next page says its relative dimension jumps from 2 to 3 there. This matches the fact that in characteristic 3 the curve with j = 0 = 1728 has a larger automorphism group (order 12), the extra automorphisms appearing 'set-theoretically'. The next page proposes cutting out a smooth subgroup scheme over Spec Z, agreeing with Z̃ over Z[1/3], via a congruence c0 + c1 ≡ 0 mod 3.
errors: The group structure on Z̃_{ρ,σ} is explicitly admitted, not proved; with the inhomogeneous term 3ν''(M)λ1, closure under composition needs a cocycle identity for ν'', which is not checked here.
Naming is inconsistent: the group is first written Z̃_{ρ,σ}, crossed out, then called N_{ρ,σ}. N^{0+} and Z̃^{+0} are used for the analogous kernels.

The claimed jump of fibre dimension at 3 is asserted without computation. With σ of order 2 or 4, (1 − σ) is invertible mod 3, so the naive rank count of the linear map (α0, β0) ↦ (1 − ρ)α0 − (1 − σ)β0 does not obviously drop. The non-smoothness must come from the precise definition of M or of ρ_M, σ_M, which cannot be verified from this page.

ideas.what: Group of twisted 1-cocycle data on the amalgam generated by ρ, σ, as an extension of the mod-12 congruence group 𝔒_12^* by a linear group scheme
ideas.modern_name: Extension built from H^1 / crossed homomorphisms of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 with lattice coefficients; affine (Heisenberg/semidirect) extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group cohomology of free products (Serre, Trees; Eichler–Shimura for cohomology of SL2(Z))
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) treats the Teichmüller tower and SL2(Z) but not, to my knowledge, this explicit group scheme

ideas.what: Rewriting the inhomogeneous condition as homogeneous via the identity (1 − ρ)(1 − ρ²) = 3
ideas.modern_name: Eisenstein-integer norm identity; change of cocycle by a coboundary

ideas.what: Observation that the resulting group scheme over Spec Z is smooth over Z[1/3] but has a jumping fibre in characteristic 3, linked to extra automorphisms of the j = 0 = 1728 curve in char 3
ideas.modern_name: Non-smooth automorphism group schemes at bad primes; Néron-type smoothening / dilatation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud, Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud (Néron models, smoothening); Deligne–Rapoport for the moduli of elliptic curves at 2 and 3

missed.claim: Grothendieck admits without proof a natural group structure on the extension Z̃_{ρ,σ} of 𝔒_12^*. On the next page he sketches a smooth sub-group-scheme over Spec Z, defined by a congruence mod 3, coinciding with Z̃ over Z[1/3]. Neither the group law nor the smoothening is carried out on this page.
missed.quote: Je vais admettre comme [?] qu'on a une structure de groupe naturelle sur Z̃_{ρ,σ} ... Le schéma en groupes est lisse en car. ≠ 3, mais pas en car. 3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small worked instance of integral (Spec Z) models of symmetry groups attached to SL2(Z) and the j = 0, 1728 curves, relevant to understanding the Teichmüller/GT action integrally. It is likely recoverable by specialists via dilatation techniques, so the novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine but careful linear-algebraic construction of an extension group scheme with a remark on bad reduction at 3. The ideas (cocycles on the amalgam, smoothening at a bad prime) are standard; the specific object may be unpublished but is not of a kind that would startle a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the crossed-out 'Z̃_{ρ,σ} ...' is replaced by 'N_{ρ,σ} et la'; the exact sequence uses N^{0+}_{ρ,σ}.
(94): the first coordinate is underlined M (an element of 𝔒_12^*), with ρ_M and σ_M indexed by it. The '‖' above the brace marks equality of Z̃_{ρ,σ} with the set.
(97): the kernel is written Z̃^{+0}_{ρ,σ} (superscript appears as '+0', with a crossed-out '*').
(98): 'dfn' over the equals sign; '≀‖' (isomorphism) marks the identification with the set of pairs (α0, β0).
Last line likely reads '... mais pas en car. 3, où sa dimension passe' (continuing 'de la dim. relative 2 à la dim. relative 3' on the next page) rather than 'il devient pas'.
